set.prevailing_wage_basis: Conduit tax-exempt bond financing (CMFA issuer, County TEFRA approval only) is not payment out of public funds under Labor Code 1720(b): DIR Decision on Administrative Appeal, Public Works Case No. 2006-020, Heber Family Apartments (April 5, 2007), following PW 2004-016 Rancho Santa Fe Village and PW 2006-005 Central Village Apartments, held that neither publicly offered nor privately placed housing revenue bonds, nor federal LIHTCs, trigger prevailing wage because the proceeds and repayments never pass through public coffers. https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/coverage/year2007/2006-020(A).pdf. Other public funds layered in the same deal (for example project-based vouchers or local loans) are evaluated separately and can trigger prevailing wage.

reason: DIR Heber Family Apartments appeal decision holds conduit housing revenue bonds are not public funds under Labor Code 1720(b), and the April 28, 2026 Board packet confirms the County is not the issuer and bears no liability.
